item.title: Reps probe SGF’s approval for lawmakers’ foreign trips
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has mandated its Committees on Public Service Matters and Legislative Compliance to investigate a circular requiring the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF) to approve official foreign trips by National Assembly presiding officers, principal officers and members. The House also reaffirmed the constitutional independence of the legislature, warning that subjecting lawmakers’ official foreign travel to executive approval could undermine the principle of separation of powers. The resolution followed a motion sponsored by Hon. Jesse Okey-Joe Onuakalusi, who drew the House’s attention to a circular dated August 13, 2026, with reference number PRS59648/5.13/TI/335, issued by the Office of the SGF. The circular reportedly requires prior approval from the SGF before the Ministry of Foreign Affairs can issue Notes Verbales for official foreign trips by National Assembly presiding officers, principal officers and members. Moving the motion, Onuakalusi expressed concern that the requirement could compromise legislative independence, impede parliamentary diplomacy and create an inappropriate system of executive control over the legislature. He maintained that the National Assembly was an independent arm of government, not a ministry, department, agency or subordinate institution of the executive. The lawmaker cited Sections 4, 5 and 6 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which establish the legislature, executive and judiciary as distinct arms of government founded on the principles of separation of powers and checks and balances. He also referenced Section 51 of the Constitution and Section 22 of the National Assembly Act, 2014, in reaffirming the legislature’s constitutional status and authority over its internal administrative arrangements. Onuakalusi stressed that executive administrative procedures must respect constitutional boundaries and should not interfere with the legislature’s ability to discharge its constitutional responsibilities. Following the adoption of the motion, the House directed the Committees on Public Service Matters and Legislative Compliance to investigate the circular and its implications for parliamentary independence. The committees are expected to recommend appropriate legislative action and report back to the House within four weeks for further consideration. The resolution reinforces the House’s position that administrative procedures introduced by the executive must not undermine the autonomy of the National Assembly or interfere with its constitutional functions. Bill, 2026, warning that the legislation could create regulatory conflicts, duplicate existing laws and disrupt legitimate businesses. NECA, in a formal submission to the Senate Committee on Health, urged the National Assembly to exclude tobacco products from the proposed legislation, arguing that the sector is already subject to a dedicated regulatory framework. The Bill, sponsored by Senator Umar Sadiq Suleiman, passed second reading in the Senate on July 21, 2026. It seeks to repeal the Food, Drugs and Related Products Act, 2004, and establish a new regulatory framework for food, medical and related products. However, NECA argued that extending the Bill’s provisions to tobacco products could conflict with the National Tobacco Control Act, 2015, the National Tobacco Control Regulations, 2019, and the Standards Organisation of Nigeria Act, 2015. According to the employers’ association, the proposed framework could create overlapping responsibilities among the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC), the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, SON and the Nigeria Customs Service. It warned that such overlaps could lead to multiple product-registration requirements, duplicated approvals, conflicting enforcement decisions, increased compliance costs and uncertainty for businesses. NECA maintained that tobacco products constitute a distinct regulatory category and should not be treated as food or medicines under the proposed law. It also argued that NAFDAC’s existing statutory mandate does not expressly cover tobacco products, adding that their inclusion in the Bill could extend the agency’s authority into an area already governed by dedicated legislation. The association further raised concerns about provisions granting additional powers over product registration, suspension, seizure, factory operations and enforcement, warning that these could conflict with the responsibilities of existing regulatory institutions. Of particular concern to NECA is the proposed ceiling-list mechanism, which it said could give NAFDAC excessive administrative discretion to restrict products without adequate statutory safeguards and oversight. The association called on lawmakers to introduce safeguards against unilateral regulatory decisions, strengthen coordination among existing institutions and amend the Bill to prevent duplication, regulatory uncertainty and unnecessary disruption to businesses. It stressed that a coherent regulatory environment was essential for investment, economic growth, effective public-health protection and compliance with the law. NECA also urged lawmakers to ensure that the proposed legislation complemented, rather than contradicted, Nigeria’s existing tobacco-control framework. The association said effective regulation should be based on clearly defined institutional responsibilities, predictable compliance requirements, proportionate enforcement and coordination among relevant government agencies. It expressed readiness to engage further with the National Assembly and other stakeholders to achieve a legislative outcome that protects public health while sustaining regulatory certainty and business confidence. Health Ministry, SON seek deferment The Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare also expressed reservations about the proposed amendments at a public hearing on the Bill. Represented by Dr Adebisi Adegoke, mni, Director of Hospital Services, the Ministry raised concerns about potential regulatory conflicts, duplication and overlapping mandates, which it said could undermine effective government administration. It recommended deferring consideration of the Bill to allow further consultations among affected stakeholders and ensure alignment with the Ministry’s existing responsibilities. SON similarly raised concerns that some provisions of the proposed legislation conflicted with the law establishing the organisation and could interfere with its statutory responsibilities. The standards body backed the call for the Bill’s consideration to be deferred, arguing that a more comprehensive review was needed to remove unnecessary complexities and overlapping mandates. It also expressed concern that the process leading to the proposed amendments had not involved sufficient engagement and consultation with affected institutions. Industry operators warn of business disruption Tobacco industry operators have also expressed reservations about the proposed legislation, warning that another layer of regulation could complicate compliance rather than improve regulatory effectiveness. At a recent public hearing, industry stakeholders argued that tobacco manufacturing, importation, distribution, packaging, health warnings, product standards and related activities were already subject to extensive statutory controls. They warned that parallel approval and enforcement structures could expose manufacturers and importers to conflicting directives, additional administrative costs, operational disruptions and uncertainty over which regulator has final authority. The operators maintained that their concerns were not about resisting public-health regulation but about the risks of multiplying regulatory requirements without clearly demonstrated public-policy benefits. They further argued that unpredictable compliance obligations could weaken investor confidence, discourage business expansion and complicate efforts by the Federal Government to improve Nigeria’s competitiveness and ease of doing business. According to the industry position, unnecessary administrative burdens on compliant businesses could also divert regulatory attention and resources from more pressing enforcement challenges, including illicit trade and non-compliant operators. item.title: Presidential Panel submits National Policing Draft, 29 Amendment Bills to Justice Ministry
item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — THE Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill has concluded the drafting phase of its assignment and formally submitted the draft National Policing Bill (2026), alongside 29 consequential amendment bills, to the Federal Ministry of Justice for legislative review and validation. The submission was made on Monday, 19th October, 2026, to the Attorney General of the Federation, AGF and Minister of Justice, in line with the Working Group’s work plan. This was revealed via a statement issued by the Chief of Staff to the President and Chairman Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill, Rt. Hon. Femi Gbajabiamila. Gbajabiamila, who was a former Speaker of the House of Representatives, explained that the Ministry’s review will ensure that the bills conform to legislative drafting standards and conventions, and that they do not conflict with existing laws. According to the statement: “The Ministry of Justice is expected to return the validated draft bills to the Working Group on or before Friday, 30th October 2026. The Working Group will then give the validated bills final consideration before presenting them to Mr President, thereby concluding its mandate. “The proposed National Policing Bill seeks to establish the constitutional and legislative framework for a dual policing structure, comprising a Federal Police Service and State Police Services.” He further said: “The Working Group remains committed to a rigorous and transparent process that will deliver a comprehensive legislative proposal for consideration by the President and subsequent transmission to the National Assembly. “The work on preparing the National Policing Bill is proceeding alongside the ongoing consideration of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026 by the States Houses of Assembly, which must be completed before the Bill is transmitted to the National Assembly.” The post Presidential Panel submits National Policing Draft, 29 Amendment Bills to Justice Ministry appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — THE Presidency on Tuesday said it is seeking to mobilise about ₦20 billion over the next four years to confront flooding, drought, desertification, migration and other climate pressures across the region. This is as the North-West Climate Summit has been described as Africa’s first regional climate marketplace. Senior Special Assistant to the President on Community Engagement (North-West), Hon. Abdullahi Tanko Yakasai, said the summit is the inaugural edition of a regional platform designed to connect states and local governments with development partners, financial institutions and investors. The initiative is being implemented with the Northern Governors’ Forum, the North-West Governors’ Forum and the North-West Development Commission. Yakasai said the summit rests on three pillars: a Climate Marketplace, a Climate Academy and a Climate Fund. He explained that the marketplace will allow subnational governments to showcase climate programmes and attract partnerships and financing from local and international institutions. “Local governments and states can go into that platform and put up what they are doing on climate change, so that international development partners, international financial institutions, and even the local ones can see what programmes they are doing on climate,” he said. He explained that the Climate Academy is expected to train 10,000 young people across the North-West on climate resilience, climate action and related areas. According to him, the Climate Fund will channel resources towards interventions on flooding, drought, renewable energy and other climate-related challenges. “That fund will be channelled through the Office of the SSA on Community Engagement to tackle those issues,” Yakasai said. item.title: NYSC kidnapping: Identities of suspects vindicate us – IPOB
item.description: …Raise questions over profiling of Igbo youths …Group demands investigation into alleged sponsors of insecurity in South-East By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — The Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) has called for a thorough investigation into the abduction of prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members along the Owerri–Onitsha Expressway in Imo State, following the arraignment of five suspects over the incident. The group said the suspects’ identities raised questions about the attribution of kidnappings and other criminal activities in the South-East to its members and the Eastern Security Network (ESN) before investigations establish those responsible. The suspects were identified as Usman Aliyu, Babangida Aliyu, Mohammed Ali, Aminu Haliru and Ibrahim Jiji. In a statement issued on Tuesday by its Media and Publicity Secretary, Comrade Emma Powerful, IPOB said the case reinforced its longstanding position that its members and ESN had been wrongly blamed for insecurity in the region. The group argued that, had the suspects not been apprehended, Igbo youths and ESN members might have been accused of the crime, potentially exposing innocent people to arrest and other alleged mistreatment. “Had this atrocious kidnapping happened without these suspects being caught, who would the Nigerian security apparatus and hostile media have blamed?” IPOB asked. The group said previous incidents in the South-East had similarly been attributed to IPOB and ESN, insisting that criminal allegations should be subjected to evidence-based investigations. IPOB maintained that its members were not responsible for kidnappings in the region, adding that ESN was established to protect communities, farmers and residents against armed attacks. The group commended the Director of the Department of State Services (DSS) in Imo State and the prosecuting team, describing the case as an opportunity to establish the facts surrounding the abduction. It called for a comprehensive investigation into the suspects’ identities, origins, networks and alleged accomplices, urging authorities to make the findings public in accordance with the law. IPOB also urged security agencies to investigate criminal activities based on evidence rather than ethnicity, political affiliation or unverified allegations. The statement renewed the group’s criticism of the continued detention of its leader, Mazi Nnamdi Kanu, arguing that his warnings about security threats in the region had not received adequate attention. IPOB further called on South-East governors and political leaders to strengthen security in rural communities and forests, protect lives and property, and ensure that innocent residents were not unfairly associated with criminal activities. item.title: Dele Giwa: NGE demands justice 40 years after murder
item.description: The Nigerian Guild of Editors (NGE) has called on relevant authorities to revisit the unresolved assassination of renowned journalist, Dele Giwa, insisting that the passage of 40 years must not extinguish the quest for justice. Giwa, co-founder of Newswatch magazine, was killed by a parcel bomb delivered to his home on October 19, 1986. Four decades after the incident, no one has been brought to justice for his murder. In a statement on Monday to mark the 40th anniversary of Giwa’s assassination, the NGE President, Eze Anaba, and General Secretary, Onuoha Ukeh, described the unresolved case as a painful test of Nigeria’s commitment to press freedom, public accountability and the rule of law. The Guild said the country could not afford to allow the case to disappear into history, stressing that the responsibility to investigate serious crimes did not expire with time or changes in government. “Forty years is a long time to wait for justice. It is an unconscionably long time for a nation that claims to uphold the rule of law,” the Guild said. It urged the appropriate authorities to revisit the case, examine credible evidence that might still be available, preserve relevant records and pursue every lawful avenue towards establishing the truth about Giwa’s death. The Guild, however, cautioned against trial by media, insisting that its demand was for a credible investigation rather than the condemnation of anyone without evidence. “We are not calling for trial by media. We are not asking anyone to be condemned without evidence. We are demanding that a grave crime against a Nigerian citizen, a distinguished journalist and the freedom of the press should not remain an enduring symbol of impunity,” it said. The NGE made the call as it highlighted the significance of a book, Dele Giwa’s Granite Journalism, unveiled on Monday to preserve the late journalist’s professional legacy. According to the NGE, Giwa understood that journalism was neither a public relations department for those in authority nor an instrument for flattering the powerful, but a public trust. It said his assassination was not merely the killing of an individual but an attack on the freedom to ask questions, expose wrongdoing and hold those in authority accountable. The Guild expressed concern that the unresolved murder could send a troubling message to journalists investigating corruption, probing abuses of power or exposing the activities of influential interests. It asked whether the passage of time, the death of witnesses or changes in government should diminish the state’s obligation to pursue justice, insisting that the answer must be no. “An unresolved murder is not a closed chapter. It is an open wound in the nation’s conscience,” it said. Beyond the demand for justice, the NGE urged contemporary journalists and editors to reflect on the state of the profession, particularly its independence from political and commercial interests. It said the principles represented by Giwa required journalists to demonstrate courage, accuracy, independence, fairness and a commitment to the truth. “Courage without accuracy can become recklessness; independence without ethics can become irresponsibility,” the Guild said, adding that journalism worth defending must be both fearless and scrupulous, independent and accountable. item.title: UCL: Bayern sweat over Kompany, Neuer, Kimmich fitness for Arsenal clash
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Bayern Munich could be without manager Vincent Kompany, goalkeeper Manuel Neuer and midfielder Joshua Kimmich for Wednesday’s Champions League clash against Arsenal, assistant coach Aaron Danks has said. According to Reuters, Danks disclosed the doubts at a press conference on Tuesday, with Kompany battling a virus, Neuer recovering from a minor injury and Kimmich missing training for personal reasons. “Vince has had a virus, and it is important for him to rest,” Danks said, adding that the manager was at home and his involvement would be assessed on a day-to-day basis. Neuer has returned to training over the past two days, but Bayern are yet to decide whether the goalkeeper will be available for the Arsenal encounter. Kimmich’s participation also remains uncertain. Bayern will also be without suspended winger Michael Olise as they seek to return to winning ways in the competition after last week’s 3-3 draw against Viking in Norway. However, the German champions head into the encounter with confidence after thrashing RB Leipzig 6-1 in the Bundesliga on Saturday. Danks said the contest would be decided by fine margins, insisting Bayern must prepare for every aspect of the game and encourage their players to perform without fear. item.title: Plateau Assembly Adopts State Police Bill, Backs Decentralised Policing
item.description: The Plateau State House of Assembly has adopted the recommendations of its Ad-hoc Committee in support of the proposed constitutional amendment to establish State Police in Nigeria. The decision was reached during Monday’s plenary session presided over by the Speaker, Naanlong Daniel, following the presentation and consideration of the committee’s report. The proposed Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, was transmitted to the 36 State Houses of Assembly on September 16, 2026, by the Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, for consideration and approval. The bill seeks to provide a constitutional framework for the establishment of State Police Services alongside the Federal Police Service as part of efforts to address Nigeria’s persistent security challenges. Presenting the committee’s report, its chairman and member representing Qua’an-Pan South Constituency, Theodore Maiyaki, said the proposed amendment was necessary in view of prevailing security challenges, manpower shortages in the Nigeria Police Force and the need to strengthen policing at the grassroots. He explained that the proposal would establish a framework for federal and state policing, with safeguards for human rights, operational standards, accountability and coordination. The committee also noted that improved security was critical to the socioeconomic development of Plateau State and the country at large, recommending that the House support the proposed constitutional alteration. Following deliberations, lawmakers adopted the recommendations and voted in support of the proposed amendment. The Speaker, Naanlong Daniel. The Speaker, Naanlong Daniel, commended the committee for its work and thanked members for their patience, commitment and sacrifice in considering the legislative proposal. The constitutional amendment requires approval by at least 24 of Nigeria’s 36 State Houses of Assembly before it can proceed to the next stage of the process. Meanwhile, the House passed two other bills for first reading: the Plateau State Right of Patients and Medical Institutions Bill and the Plateau State Bill on Jungle Justice, Mob Action and Other Forms of Unlawful Violence Against Persons. The bills will undergo further legislative consideration in line with the rules of the Assembly. The House subsequently resolved to proceed on recess from Monday, October 19, to Tuesday, November 10, 2026, to allow members to rest and prepare for upcoming legislative responsibilities. The Speaker appreciated lawmakers, supporting staff, and other personnel for their dedication to the service of Plateau State, noting that the Assembly had continued its legislative duties beyond the initially scheduled recess period.
